subtopics.title: Force Without Touching — the Idea of a Field

questions.question: A magnetic field is defined as:
options: A beam of magnetism travelling from north to south
A region in space where another magnet or a ferromagnetic material experiences a force
The metal core inside a magnet
An electric current flowing around a magnet

questions.question: Gravitational, electric and magnetic fields respectively act on:
options: Charge, mass, and poles
Mass, poles, and charge
Mass, charge, and magnets or ferromagnetic materials
All three act on anything made of metal

questions.question: Which set of materials is ferromagnetic?
options: Iron, steel, cobalt and nickel
Copper, aluminium and brass
Glass, plastic and wood
All metals without exception

questions.question: A magnet holds a paper note against a steel cupboard door because:
options: Paper is weakly ferromagnetic
The magnet electrifies the paper
The door pushes the paper outward
Paper is invisible to the field, and the force acts between magnet and steel through it

subtopics.title: Poles Come in Pairs — and the Pair Cannot Be Divorced

questions.question: The interaction rule for magnetic poles is:
options: All poles attract each other
Like poles repel; opposite poles attract
Like poles attract; opposite poles repel
Poles only interact when touching

questions.question: Sawing a bar magnet in half produces:
options: One pure north piece and one pure south piece
Two unmagnetised pieces of steel
Two complete magnets, each with its own north and south pole
One strong magnet and one weak one

questions.question: In an unmagnetised steel nail, the magnetic domains:
options: Point in random directions and cancel each other out
All point toward the nail's tip
Do not exist until a magnet touches it
Are aligned but too weak to notice

questions.question: Stroking a steel needle repeatedly with a magnet in one direction magnetises it because the strokes:
options: Heat the needle up
Transfer north material into the needle
Electrically charge the needle
Align more and more of the needle's domains in the same direction

subtopics.title: Drawing the Invisible — Magnetic Field Lines

questions.question: Outside a magnet, field lines are drawn:
options: From south pole to north pole
From north pole to south pole, with arrows
In circles around the middle of the magnet
Only inside the metal

questions.question: Closely crowded field lines in a diagram indicate:
options: A weak region of the field
A drawing error
A strong region of the field
The field is three-dimensional there

questions.question: Iron filings sprinkled over a bar magnet reveal:
options: The shape of the field pattern, but not its direction
The direction of the field, but not its shape
Both the shape and the direction of the field
Nothing unless a current also flows

questions.question: Two like poles face each other. The field diagram shows:
options: A dense bridge of lines connecting the two poles
Lines crossing between the poles
Lines spiralling around both magnets
Lines bending away from the gap, with a neutral point between the poles

questions.question: A compass works because its needle is:
options: A small magnet that aligns with the field it sits in
Electrically charged by the atmosphere
Heavier at its north end
Attracted to cold air in the north

questions.question: The Earth's magnetic pole in the northern hemisphere behaves magnetically like:
options: A north pole, since needles point at it
A south pole, since it attracts the north end of compass needles
Both poles at once
Neither — it carries electric charge instead

questions.question: The geographic North Pole and the magnetic north pole are:
options: The same fixed point
Always exactly opposite each other
Hundreds of kilometres apart, with the magnetic pole drifting over the years
Both moving with the seasons

questions.question: The auroras near the poles are caused by:
options: Sunlight reflecting off the ice caps
Lightning storms in the upper atmosphere
Moonlight bent by the magnetic field
Solar-wind particles funnelled along field lines striking the upper atmosphere

questions.question: The magnet grabs the steel door just before touching it because:
options: Its field — a bubble of influence — reaches across the air gap
Static electricity jumps the gap
Air pushes the magnet forward
The door is slightly sticky

questions.question: The magnetic bubble is strongest:
options: Everywhere equally
Right at the magnet, fading quickly with distance
About a metre away from the magnet
Only when the magnet is moving

questions.question: Which kitchen object would a magnet grip?
options: An aluminium pot
A copper wire
A pair of steel scissors
A wooden spoon

questions.question: Snipping a magnetised pin in half to keep only its north end:
options: Works if the cut is exactly in the middle
Leaves the north half unmagnetised
Destroys the magnetism completely
Fails — the cut face grows a new south pole, making two complete magnets

questions.question: In the stadium-crowd picture, a magnetised pin is like a crowd:
options: All doing the wave in time — domains aligned in one direction
Sitting perfectly still
Doing random movements that cancel out
Leaving the stadium

questions.question: Dropping a magnet hard on concrete weakens it because the shock:
options: Chips off the north pole
Knocks some domains out of alignment
Cools the magnet down
Lets electrons escape from the metal

questions.question: A magnetic monopole — a lone north or south pole — is:
options: Common inside strong magnets
Made whenever a magnet is cut
Something no laboratory has ever observed
The core of the Earth

questions.question: A magnetised needle floating on cork settles north-south because:
options: Water currents push it that way
The cork is heavier at one end
Wind aligns it along the bowl
It aligns with the Earth's magnetic field like any magnet in a field

questions.question: Navigators must correct between the two norths because:
options: The magnetic pole lies hundreds of kilometres from the geographic pole and drifts
Maps are drawn around the magnetic pole
The geographic pole moves with the core's molten iron
Compasses point south in winter

questions.question: The Earth's magnetic field protects life by:
options: Warming the atmosphere at night
Deflecting most of the solar wind around the planet
Blocking sunlight at the poles
Holding the oceans in place

questions.question: A violent solar eruption that rattles the Earth's field can cause:
options: Earthquakes along fault lines
Permanent loss of the auroras
A magnetic storm that disrupts radio, satellites and power grids
The compass needles to stop working forever
